# Getting started with Duck.ai: a beginner's guide to private AI chat

> **In short:** Duck.ai is DuckDuckGo's AI chat, and you can start a conversation without making an account. DuckDuckGo says it does not use your chats to train its AI models. Still, treat it as a helpful tool, not a vault: never type passwords, bank details or private medical records into any chat.

You will learn how to open Duck.ai, start your first chat without signing up, write a message the AI can actually help with, and understand what DuckDuckGo's privacy promises mean in everyday terms. This guide is for anyone who is curious about AI chatbots but would rather not hand over an account or a pile of personal details to try one out.

## Before you start

- **A web browser or the DuckDuckGo app.** Any modern browser on a phone, tablet or computer will work. You can go straight to the Duck.ai website.
- **An internet connection.** Duck.ai runs online, so it won't work offline.
- **No account needed.** This is the whole point of this guide. If a sign-in screen appears, you can usually keep going without one.
- **About 10 minutes.** Plan on reading and trying each step once.

## Step 1 — Open Duck.ai

Open your web browser and type **duck.ai** into the address bar at the top. Press Enter. You should land on a simple page with a message box near the bottom, where you type your questions. The page is designed to be clean, so you may see little else besides a short introduction and a few suggested topics.

If you already use the DuckDuckGo app or its browser, look for an option to open the AI chat there. The exact spot can change, so search the app's menu for "Duck.ai" or look for a chat or AI-style icon. Both routes lead to the same chat.

**If it looks different:** the website may show a notice about how Duck.ai works, or ask you to accept terms. Read it briefly, then look for a button that lets you continue. Those notices are normal and you only need to deal with them once.

You'll know it worked when you see an empty chat with a message box at the bottom and nothing asking you to sign in.

## Step 2 — Start a chat without an account

Stay on the Duck.ai page and look at the message box. You do not need to create a username, enter an email address or choose a password to begin. The chat is ready as soon as the page loads. Think of it like walking into a public library reading room: you can sit down and start reading without a membership card, although some rooms have rules you should know about.

If you see a prompt asking you to sign in or subscribe, look for a button or link that says you can continue without doing so, or simply close the prompt and return to the message box. Some features, such as higher usage limits, may need a paid plan, so check the official Duck.ai site for current details before you rely on any particular feature.

**If it looks different:** sometimes Duck.ai shows a list of suggested topics above the message box. You can ignore those and type your own question.

You'll know it worked when you can click into the message box and see a blinking cursor, ready for your first message.

## Step 3 — Type your first question

Click into the message box, type your question, and press Enter (or tap the send arrow next to the box, if you see one). Your message appears in the chat as a bubble. After a moment, the answer starts appearing below it, usually one word or line at a time. This is the AI generating its reply, which can take a few seconds.

Keep your first question simple and specific. Vague questions get vague answers. Try swapping in your own details wherever you see square brackets, and remember to leave out anything private.

💬 Example: "Give me three simple dinner ideas I can cook in under 30 minutes for [number] people, using [two ingredients you have]."

**If it looks different:** if nothing happens after you press Enter, check that you're connected to the internet, then try again. If the answer doesn't appear at all, refresh the page and retype your question.

You'll know it worked when your message shows up in the chat and a reply starts appearing beneath it.

## Step 4 — Ask a follow-up to refine the answer

Read the reply carefully. If it's almost right but too long, too basic or aimed at the wrong person, type a follow-up in the same message box. The chat remembers what you said earlier in this conversation, so you don't need to repeat everything. It's like talking to a helper across a table: you can say "make it shorter" and they know what "it" means.

Follow-ups work best when they name one change at a time. A clear request gives a clear result.

💬 Example: "Thanks. Make these ideas shorter, and add one tip for a beginner who has never cooked [dish type]."

**If it looks different:** if the chat feels confused or the answers drift off topic, start a new chat for a fresh subject. Look for a "new chat" button or a plus-style icon near the top or side of the page. Starting over is a normal habit and doesn't break anything.

You'll know it worked when the new reply reflects your change, such as being shorter or including the beginner tip.

## Step 5 — Understand what the privacy promises mean for you

This step matters most. DuckDuckGo built Duck.ai around privacy, and it says publicly that it does not use your chats to train its AI models. Think of training as the AI studying what people write so it can improve. DuckDuckGo's position is that your conversations aren't used for that study. It also says it removes identifying details, such as your IP address, before sending your chats to the AI companies whose models it offers. Check DuckDuckGo's own privacy pages for the exact current wording, because policies can be updated.

Privacy promises are not the same as secrecy. A few things still apply. Your chat is still processed by a service, so don't type anything you would be upset to see leaked. Look for a settings or menu icon on the page to see whether you can clear your chat history. If you see that option, it's a good way to tidy up after a conversation you'd rather not keep.

💬 Example: "Help me write a short thank-you note to my neighbor for watering my plants while I was away."

**If it looks different:** privacy settings may be tucked under a menu, behind a gear icon, or in a separate section about your data. If you can't find them, search DuckDuckGo's help or privacy pages for "Duck.ai" instead of guessing.

You'll know it worked when you have located the chat history or privacy options and understand that the safest habit is simply not typing sensitive details in the first place.

## Common mistakes

- **Typing sensitive information.** Passwords, Social Security numbers, bank logins and private medical details should never go into any AI chat, even one with strong privacy promises. The fix: describe the situation in general terms instead, such as "a bill I need to dispute" rather than your account number.
- **Trusting the answer without checking it.** AI can sound confident and still be wrong. The fix: verify important facts, especially health, money or legal questions, with a trusted source or a professional.
- **Expecting it to remember you forever.** Duck.ai is built for quick, private chats, so it doesn't work like a personal assistant who knows your life. It also can't open your files or see your screen unless a feature clearly says it can. The fix: paste in the details you need for each conversation.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** Use Duck.ai to plan a weekend trip, draft a birthday message, or explain a confusing paragraph from a recipe or manual. Keep the details general and you'll get useful help without over-sharing.
- **For your business or work:** Use it to brainstorm email subject lines, summarize a public article you've already read, or practice a difficult conversation. Don't paste confidential client, employee or company information, and check your employer's policy before using any AI tool for work.
- **If you're just getting started:** Begin with one low-stakes question, like a recipe or a gift idea. Once you see how the chat responds, you'll understand the rhythm and feel more comfortable with the tool.

## Try it now

Open **duck.ai** in your browser, type "Suggest three easy weekend activities for [your city] in [season]," and press Enter. When the reply appears, type one follow-up asking it to make the list shorter. You'll have used Duck.ai without an account in under two minutes.
